rubric_items.reason: countByStatus, service status_counts and the counts line/links are tested; the new 21-appointment test closes the paging gap (prior F-1). S-4 AC3 (patient list rows and total follow a date-range change) still has no dedicated assertion.
Assertions check exact count objects, key order, sum vs total, 20/1 row split with the 21st id and status on page 2, exact rendered line and link query params.

Zero counts, no matches, other doctor/patient, local-day exclusion, status replacement, 400 invalid status and failed fetch are covered; the inclusion side of the day boundary still uses an 11:45 slot, not late evening.
Vitest+Supertest with own fresh database and injected clock for API; Vitest+jsdom+Testing Library with stubbed fetch and MemoryRouter for web; names carry HMS-30 REQ-n.
No pass or coverage numbers are stated; results are deferred to checks.json and the artifact notes the verifier skips coverage, matching the coverage step status skip.

findings.text: S-4 is listed as covered, but S-4 AC3 (a patient list's rows and total follow a date-range change) has no test: the patient-list test uses one range and checks counts only, never total or rows after a range change.

cites.quote: Given a patient's list, when staff change the date range filter, then the table rows and the total change to the new range as before the change.
S-4: covered by the API 20-row paging, order/envelope and invalid-status tests and the web table/filter test.
const p1 = await list({ patientId: '1', from: MONDAY, to: TUESDAY });

findings.suggested_fix: Add a patient-list test that lists two ranges (e.g. MONDAY..MONDAY then MONDAY..TUESDAY) and asserts total, row count and sum of counts each time; or narrow the S-4 Known line.

findings.text: Prior F-3 unchanged: the local-day boundary inclusion case is a Tuesday 11:45 midday slot, not the late-evening 23:30 local case S-2 AC2 describes, so the inclusion side of the edge is weaker than the story.

findings.suggested_fix: Insert a 23:30 local appointment on the last day directly (as done for Wednesday 01:00) and assert it is counted.
